en: The moon's gravity pulls ocean water to create high and low tides along Philippine beaches.
Heavy rain reduces friction between soil and rock, causing landslides on the steep slopes of the Cordillera mountains.
A naturally sloping riverbank acts as an inclined plane, making it easier to walk down to the water.
The Earth acts like a giant magnet, causing compass needles to point north during hikes in the Sierra Madre.
Friction between ice particles inside thunderclouds creates static electricity that discharges as lightning over Manila Bay.
Sunlight refracts inside raindrops after a tropical monsoon rain to form a rainbow over the Banaue rice terraces.
Shouting in the deep ravines of the Chocolate Hills produces an echo because sound waves reflect off the rocks.
Barefoot walking on Boracay's white sand at noon feels hot because the sand absorbs radiant heat from the sun.
The Mayon Volcano releases thermal energy from deep inside the Earth, heating underground water to produce natural hot springs.
The strong, growing roots of banyan trees act as wedges that slowly split apart large rocks in the soil.
A falling coconut accelerates toward the ground due to the gravitational pull of the Earth on its mass.
Daytime land heats faster than the sea, causing convection currents that create a cool sea breeze in coastal towns.
